advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm select_from_corpus's default env-mutating ticket-state reader is safe for its intended (single-threaded) callers, or thread the tracker path explicitly instead of via os.environ.
evidence: labels.py:290: `os.environ["REBAR_TRACKER_DIR"] = tracker_path` — process-global mutation per call
fixture_selection.py:447-448: reader invoked in a `for review in reviews` loop
advisory.finding: select_from_corpus's default ticket-state reader (_read_ticket_state_via_env_override) mutates os.environ['REBAR_TRACKER_DIR'] process-wide inside the per-review enrichment loop, so it is not safe under concurrent selection and leaks/relies on global mutable state; the corpus determinism test uses this default path.
scenarios: Two select_from_corpus runs (or any other rebar code reading REBAR_TRACKER_DIR) executing concurrently in the same process

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a select_from_corpus test that omits criteria_ids to exercise the _default_criteria routing/eval-spec filter path.
evidence: ABSENCE: no test calls select_from_corpus without criteria_ids, so _default_criteria and its _has_eval_spec filter are untested.
advisory.finding: The select_from_corpus default-criteria branch (criteria_ids=None -> _default_criteria via effective_routing + _has_eval_spec filtering) is never exercised: both corpus tests pass an explicit criteria_ids=[_CRITERION], so the added routing/eval-spec filter logic has no regression coverage.
scenarios: A regression in effective_routing filtering or _has_eval_spec would silently select the wrong criteria set in production, where criteria_ids is not supplied.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where one criterion yields both a fire candidate and a no_fire candidate, asserting both directions' rows and their independent 0-based ranks.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_selection.py: `admitted = fire + no_fire` where fire and no_fire are each _rank()'d independently starting at rank 0
ABSENCE: no-fire tests (test_no_fire_admitted_only_when_routed_and_uncited) and fire tests never co-occur for the same criterion in one review set.
advisory.finding: No test covers a single criterion producing BOTH a fire candidate and a no_fire candidate, so the fire+no_fire concatenation and their independent rank-from-0 sequences in select_candidates are unverified.
scenarios: A criterion that both fires (a cited norm_id) and has a routed-silent absence-consensus candidate would exercise the concatenation + dual rank sequence, currently untested.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix last_rubric_commit_ts vintage gate so a packaged rubric outside repo_root is git-logged against the committed catalog location (or documented/asserted to require an editable install).
evidence: prompts.py:119: `return files("rebar.llm").joinpath("reviewers")` — the packaged catalog dir
fixture_selection.py:105: `git ... log -1 --format=%ct base_ref -- logged_path` — an absolute path outside repo_root matches no committed history → empty stdout → None
The corpus E2E test only sets `repo_root = worktree root` (editable install), never exercising a site-packages catalog path
blocking.finding: The default vintage gate silently maps every PACKAGED-rubric criterion to 'no-committed-prompt-history' whenever rebar is installed as a wheel (packaged catalog outside repo_root). rubric_path returns a path under _catalog_dir()=files('rebar.llm')/'reviewers'; last_rubric_commit_ts then does path.resolve().relative_to(repo_root) which raises ValueError, falls back to the absolute out-of-repo path, and git-logs it — matching nothing — so it returns None. Only an editable/source install (where the catalog lives under src/ inside the worktree) produces committed history.
scenarios: Running select_from_corpus / the default vintage gate against a pip/wheel-installed rebar where reviewers/ lives in site-packages, not under repo_root

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish git/ref/resolution failure from a genuine empty-history result in the vintage gate (e.g. verify base_ref exists / surface a distinct error) rather than collapsing both to the same zero-row reason.
evidence: fixture_selection.py:110-111: `except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError, FileNotFoundError, PromptNotFound): return None`
fixture_selection.py:114-115: `if not text: return None` (also None on empty capture)
select_candidates emits `reason="no-committed-prompt-history"` for any None, per the docstring: 'no committed rubric history / absent base ref / git err'
The verdict None is produced both when the check ran-and-found-nothing and when the check never ran (git error / bad base_ref)
dropped.finding: last_rubric_commit_ts cannot distinguish 'git failed to run / base_ref absent / rubric_path errored' from 'the rubric genuinely has no committed history': all collapse to None, which select_candidates turns into the identical 'no-committed-prompt-history' zero row. A misconfigured base_ref, a git invocation failure, or a resolution error is therefore invisible — reported as a clean 'no history' verdict.
scenarios: A CI run where origin/main is not fetched (shallow clone) — every criterion silently reports no-committed-prompt-history rather than surfacing the missing ref
